references.text: Jesus says that "all things have been handed over to me by my Father" – a direct parallel to the Father having given all things into the Son's hand ([ref:Matt 11:27|Matthew 11:27]).
Jesus declares that "all authority in heaven and on earth has been given to me", expressing the same authority the Father has given the Son ([ref:Matt 28:18|Matthew 28:18]).
The Father loves the Son and shows him everything he himself does – this confirms the loving relationship between the Father and the Son described in John 3:35 ([ref:John 5:20|John 5:20]).
Jesus knew that the Father had given all things into his hands – an almost word-for-word repetition of "πάντα δέδωκεν ἐν τῇ χειρὶ αὐτοῦ" ([ref:John 13:3|John 13:3]).

Jesus says in his high priestly prayer that the Father has given him authority over all people – an elaboration on the fact that all things have been given into the Son's hand ([ref:John 17:2|John 17:2]).
The Father loves the Son because he gives up his life – this again shows the Father's love (ἀγαπᾷ) for the Son mentioned in John 3:35 ([ref:John 10:17|John 10:17]).
God put all things under Christ's feet and gave him as head over all things – an elaboration on the fact that all things have been given into the Son's hand ([ref:Eph 1:22|Ephesians 1:22]).
God has appointed the Son as heir of all things – this corresponds to the Father having given all things into the Son's hand ([ref:Heb 1:2|Hebrews 1:2]).
Paul says that God has put all things under Christ's feet, which expresses the same truth about the Son's universal dominion ([ref:1 Cor 15:27|1 Corinthians 15:27]).

God says to his Anointed One: "You are my son" and promises to give him the nations as an inheritance – an Old Testament background for the Father's gift of all things to the Son ([ref:Ps 2:7-8|Psalms 2:7-8]).
The Son of Man is given dominion, glory, and a kingdom from the Ancient of Days – a prophetic vision that all authority is given to the Son ([ref:Dan 7:14|Daniel 7:14]).
